title: Hold It Against Me
subtitle: 48 Holding Ways for You

description.main: A 2026 zine from the Tokyo imprint yoyogi facsimile that collects 48 instruction-manual drawings of people holding cameras, taken from the booklets packed with film cameras between the 1970s and 1990s, and pairs them with a short piece of original flash fiction.
description.extended:
Hold It Against Me is a 2026 zine from the Tokyo imprint yoyogi facsimile that collects 48 instruction-manual drawings of people holding cameras, taken from the booklets packed with film cameras between the 1970s and 1990s.

The drawings run one or two to a page in black and white on thin newsprint-like stock, with a short piece of original flash fiction set alongside them. Each figure demonstrates a grip or stance for a compact or SLR camera, and the cover figure carries the cross that manuals used to flag a wrong hold. The maker found the images while digging through old cameras in Tokyo and credits the anonymous illustrators who drew them. Fifty-two pages, ink-jet printed, staple-bound at 18.2 by 13 cm, with a cover on 80 gsm yellow paper and text in English and Japanese.

yoyogi facsimile is both the artist's name and the imprint, and this is the only title listed under it in Printed Matter's catalogue, which stocked the zine in 2026.

notes: Acquired from Printed Matter, New York: https://www.printedmatter.org/catalog/71238. Not signed. Cover line "48 Holding Ways for You" appears on the front cover and as the subtitle in the Printed Matter record. Monochrome ink-jet interior on newsprint-like paper; cover on 80 gsm yellow paper. No ISBN. Artist and publisher are the same name, yoyogi facsimile, styled lowercase; Printed Matter lists no other titles under it and no other public source for the maker was found.
